If the radius of a circle is tripled, its area becomes:
questions.explanation: Original area = πr². New radius = 3r. New area = π(3r)² = 9πr² = 9 × original area. Area scales as the square of the radius. Compare: circumference only triples when radius triples.

questions.question: A circular plate has radius 14 cm. A square hole of side 7 cm is cut from its centre. Remaining area (π = 22/7) =
questions.explanation: Circle area = π×14² = (22/7)×196 = 616 cm². Square = 7×7 = 49 cm². Remaining = 616 − 49 = 567 cm².

questions.question: A football field has two semicircular ends, each with diameter 70 m, and a rectangular middle section 100 m × 70 m. Total area (π = 22/7) =
questions.explanation: Two semicircles = one full circle with radius 35 m. Circle area = π×35² = (22/7)×1,225 = 22×175 = 3,850 m². Rectangle = 100×70 = 7,000 m². Total = 3,850 + 7,000 = 10,850 m².

questions.question: Compare: Circle with radius 7 cm vs Square with side 14 cm. Which has greater area?
questions.explanation: Circle: π×7² = 154 cm². Square: 14×14 = 196 cm². The square has greater area (196 > 154). Note: the square's side equals the circle's diameter.
